title: Spicy Grilled Nakji Octopus
shortDescription: Small octopus is coated in a spicy gochujang-garlic seasoning and grilled quickly in a perforated pan until lightly charred and opaque.
culturalContext: Nakji is commonly translated as long-arm octopus. Korean nakji dishes include stir-fried, raw, and grilled preparations; this locked grilled version is an editorial adaptation requiring species and naming review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Outdoor grill or manufacturer-approved indoor electric grill
Fish basket, perforated grill pan, or narrow-spaced grate

allergenNotes: molluscan shellfish classification and labeling require review

instructions.heading: Inspect and thaw safely
instructions.action: Inspect refrigerated or properly thawed octopus; reject damaged packaging or any sour, rancid, fishy, or ammonia odor.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Octopus smells mild and is cold, with intact flesh.
instructions.safetyNote: Reject sour, rancid, fishy, or ammonia odors and damaged or temperature-abused packages.

instructions.heading: Clean and dry
instructions.action: Follow the seller’s cleaning state and package directions; remove any remaining beak and internal material if qualified to do so, rinse briefly only as needed, and dry thoroughly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The required cleaning is complete and surfaces are dry.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep raw seafood and its juices off ready-to-eat foods; wash hands and sanitize tools afterward.

instructions.heading: Season under refrigeration
instructions.action: Combine the spicy seasoning, coat the octopus lightly, cover, and refrigerate for 20 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: A thin coating covers the octopus without pooling.
instructions.safetyNote: Keep seafood refrigerated until the grill is ready.

instructions.heading: Prepare the grill
instructions.action: Preheat a perforated grill pan or fine-mesh basket over medium-high heat and oil it lightly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The surface is hot, clean, and lightly oiled.
instructions.safetyNote: Never use a fuel-burning grill indoors; follow appliance ventilation instructions.

instructions.heading: Grill and verify
instructions.action: Drain heavy excess seasoning, spread in one layer, and grill quickly while turning until opaque, firm, lightly charred, and 145°F / 63°C in representative thick portions.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Flesh is opaque and firm, suckers are lightly charred, and representative thick portions reach 145°F / 63°C.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean thermometer and clean tools after the final turn; verify 145°F / 63°C in the thickest edible portion.

instructions.heading: Serve safely
instructions.action: Move to a clean platter, cut with clean tools if needed, and serve promptly.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The seafood is on a clean platter and served promptly.
instructions.safetyNote: Cephalopods can be chewy and pose a choking risk; cut into manageable pieces for the diner.

grillSetup: Use an outdoor grill or approved indoor electric grill with a perforated pan or fine-mesh basket over medium-high heat; oil lightly and prevent small pieces from falling through.
targetInternalTemperature: 145°F / 63°C in the thickest edible portion; visual cues supplement but do not replace thermometer verification.
visualDonenessCues: Flesh changes from translucent to opaque
Exterior is lightly charred without burned sugar
foodSafetyNotes: Buy seafood cold and keep at or below 40°F / 4°C.
Thaw only under refrigeration or a safe rapid method.
Cook to 145°F / 63°C and cut chewy pieces appropriately.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains octopus plus soy, wheat/gluten, and sesame; U.S. molluscan-shellfish classification and exact label handling require qualified review.

substitutions: Do not substitute a different cephalopod without retesting cleaning, cook time, allergen language, and texture.
ingredientSourcing: Buy cleaned octopus from a reputable seafood counter or sealed frozen package; verify species, origin, cleaning state, and allergen label.
makeAhead: Mix seasoning up to 2 days ahead; clean and season seafood only within the stated refrigerated window.
storage: Refrigerate cooked seafood in a shallow covered container within 2 hours and use within 3 days pending food-safety approval.
reheating: Reheat only the needed portion to 165°F / 74°C until steaming; avoid repeated reheating.
leftovers: Use properly refrigerated leftovers within the approved window; discard table-exposed portions after unsafe holding.
servingSuggestions: Serve promptly with rice and fresh banchan.

faq.question: Why use a grill basket?
faq.answer: It keeps small tentacles from falling through while allowing surface browning.

faq.question: Why is allergen review still required?
faq.answer: Octopus classification and labeling language must be confirmed for the intended jurisdiction.

buyingCues: Product is refrigerated on ice or frozen solid in intact packaging.
Odor is fresh and mild, never sour, rancid, fishy, or ammonia-like.
Seller identifies species, origin, and cleaning state.
seafoodPreparation.thawing: Thaw overnight in a covered container in the refrigerator. For rapid thawing, seal in a leakproof bag under cold water and cook immediately; never thaw on the counter.
seafoodPreparation.cleaningOrShellPreparation: Confirm whether the head cavity, beak, and internal material were removed; follow package or fishmonger directions and do not improvise unfamiliar live-animal processing.
seafoodPreparation.drying: Pat every surface thoroughly dry with disposable paper towels; immediately discard towels and sanitize the work area.
seafoodPreparation.scoringOrSkewering: Leave small octopus whole or separate into large manageable sections only after qualified cleaning; cutting plan requires test cooking.
seafoodPreparation.grillSurfacePreparation: Preheat and lightly oil a perforated grill pan or fine-mesh basket.
seafoodPreparation.stickingPrevention: Dry thoroughly, use a thin oil film, and turn only after the surface releases.
seafoodPreparation.approximateTime: 8 minutes, subject to product size and grill output; thermometer verification controls.
donenessCues: Flesh changes from translucent to opaque
Exterior is lightly charred without burned sugar
crossContactNotes: Use a dedicated board and tools for raw seafood.
Wash hands with soap and water after raw-seafood contact.
Use a clean thermometer, tools, and platter for cooked seafood.
